page: Microsoft Azure E2bds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.8 GHz. The instance is configured with 1 physical core that provides 2 dedicated vCPUs via multithreading. It includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for vector extensions like AVX-512 and cryptographic offloads including AES-NI and SHA-NI.

Hardware resource allocations feature 16.0 GB of system RAM, resulting in an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio that fulfills memory-optimized workload profiles. The instance includes an 81 GB local SSD for temporary scratch space or swap, while lacking onboard GPU accelerators. Network configurations omit complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring dedicated Azure networking resources for public endpoints.

Benchmark measurements indicate solid single-threaded performance offset by predictable multi-core throughput constraints resulting from its 2 vCPU profile. Single-core stress-ng reached 1889.79, and Geekbench single-core hit 1529.0, both falling within middle percentiles. Conversely, parallel execution tasks such as multi-core stress-ng (1932.98), multi-core Geekbench (1774.0), and Clang software compilation (2068.0) placed in lower percentiles due to core limitations. Memory read-only bandwidth registered at 14.85 GB/sec for uncached blocks, and Redis SET throughput recorded 2.01 million operations per second.

Given its high memory-to-core ratio and bundled local SSD storage, the E2bds_v5 provides cost-efficient hosting for medium-demand applications where memory headroom takes precedence over parallel computing power. Best-fit use cases include in-memory caching systems, small-scale relational databases, light enterprise application backends, and microservices requiring generous memory footprints without heavy compute contention.
